value.body: A two-year master's degree covering political theory, Indian government and politics, comparative politics, international relations and public administration. It is a common base for teaching, research, journalism, policy work and civil-services preparation. Many universities offer it in regular and distance modes.

items.label: PG students in political science
items.note: All PG courses in the subject
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 13, PG level, actual responses (Ministry of Education)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree, usually in any stream (some universities prefer a BA with political science). Central universities and many others admit through CUET-PG; other universities use their own entrance tests or graduation marks. Distance and open universities admit with fewer conditions.

value.title: At a glance
items: A large number of students take it, so the degree alone does not set you apart.
Teaching in colleges usually needs UGC-NET (and for many posts a PhD); UGC-NET JRF also funds a PhD.
Policy, think-tank and research roles tend to value writing samples, internships and research skills.
